stem.en: Kabir says: "If sucrose is glucose plus fructose, then sucrose should weigh the same as a glucose and a fructose together." What does the balance say?

text.en: Sucrose weighs 18 units less: one water molecule was lost when the link formed. 180 plus 180 minus 18 is 342.

feedback.en: Nothing was added, but something left. One water, mass 18, escaped as the link formed.

text.en: More, because a link weighs something.

feedback.en: A link is a shared pair of electrons around an oxygen already counted. It weighs nothing extra, and the water that left weighs 18.
The molar mass from III.2 handles it. A mole of sucrose is 342 g.

explanation.en: Condensation loses one water per link. Subtract 18 for every link when you weigh a joined molecule.
